messages:
ana: starting a canary wave to validate admission/backpressure in eu-west-1 GPU pool — wave config: 1.5k req/s sustained, 10m, 32k token cap per req. kicking off now.
ops-bot: canary-job-472 started by ana (wave=1500, region=eu-west-1) :rocket:
devon: copying the dashboard link: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/queueing?orgId=1
chet: FYI last run we saw enqueue depth hit ~4200 and p99 token latency spiked to 2.1s when admission hits 85% util. watch the admission_reject_rate metric.
maria: can we reduce admission token-bucket to 250/s for the canary? last time bucket=350/s let too many in and caused long tail.
nana: (typo) — ignore
liam: past run snippet from the agent logs where backpressure kicked in:
```
2025-11-09T14:12:03Z INFO admission: enqueue_time_ms=210 bucket_tokens=42 in_flight=1280 queue_depth=4120 reject=false
2025-11-09T14:12:04Z WARN admission: enqueue_time_ms=480 bucket_tokens=12 in_flight=1348 queue_depth=4510 reject=true reason=queue_cap
2025-11-09T14:12:05Z ERROR runtime: stall detected shard=3 gpu_util=98.3% kvcache_miss=0.12
```
devon: thanks, liam. if queue_cap triggered, we should tune the queue cap down for canary so we see graceful rejects earlier (fail-fast) not huge queueing. set queue_cap=1200?
chet: agree. propose this canary config: `{ "bucket_rate": 250, "queue_cap": 1200, "admission_policy": "regional-priority" }` — we'll run 3 waves: ramp, steady, spike.
maria: +1. also enable the new backpressure telemetry (enqueue_histogram & rejected_reasons) for this run so we can slice by shard and model.
nana: oops again (ignore)
ops-bot: telemetry-toggle: enqueue_histogram=ON, rejected_reasons=ON for canary-job-472
ana: (lol)
ana2: (two typos earlier are from my phone)
devon: quick check — what SLO should we validate? target p95 < 300ms for accept path, reject path should fail within 120ms.
nana3: (stop)
chet: ok p95 accept <300ms, p99 <800ms. Fail-fast rejects <150ms. We'll capture tail with flamegraphs if stall > 1s.
liam: running loadgen now with the proposed config, wave 1 ramp 0->1.5k over 90s. I'll post a short summary at 5m, 10m, and on finish.
maria: if regional capacity hits soft limit, remember the smart-routing fallback will redirect to dedicated pool in us-west-2 — that will affect cost. track cross-region_fallback_count.
nana: noted
ops-bot: canary-job-472 status: wave1 ramp complete, current q_depth=890, gpu_util avg=74%
devon: nice. starting to nudge bucket_rate down to 200 to see where rejects begin.
liam: wave2 steady started (1500 req/s). immediate increase in queue depth to 1.1k and admission_reject_rate=2.8%
chet: that's within our hypothesis. watch enqueue_time tail — if p99 > 600ms we abort.
liam: p95 accept=220ms, p99 accept=610ms, reject latency median=85ms. cross-region_fallback_count=0.
maria: good. drop bucket_rate to 180 and retry spike after a 2m cool-down. also tag logs with run_id=canary472-2025-11-09 so we can grep.
devon: after spike we should run a small replay against a pinned model variant with quantization to validate kernel selection under pressure.
chet: agreed. queue_cap=1200 seems to produce observable fail-fast behavior without catastrophic queuing. we can recommend this as new default for canaries.
nana: can we add a short note to the playbook: "If queue_depth > 2k and gpu_util >95% then trigger operator alert and set admission bucket to 100/s"?
maria: yes, add that. also cost note — if fallback triggers to dedicated cross-region it increases token cost by ~1.6x for the run. include in run summary.
liam: finishing spike run now. final numbers will be uploaded to the incident bucket when complete.
ops-bot: canary-job-472 finished: result=partial-success waves=3 rejects=432 peak_queue=1189 p95_accept=235ms p99_accept=628ms cross_region_fallback=0
ana: great job all. next steps: draft a short RFC to propose default canary admission profile (bucket=200, queue_cap=1200, telemetry=on) and schedule a follow-up run in ap-southeast-1 to validate region differences.
chet: i'll start the RFC. tagging @maria for cost calc. :thumbsup:
devon: thanks team.
